transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Liam Carter (Redwood SE), Sofia Mendes (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (QuartzWave VP Partnerships), Marco Velasquez (QuartzWave Head Cloud Eng), Priya Nair (QuartzWave Solutions Architect), Evan Cho (QuartzWave Procurement)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
QuartzWave is an SI/reseller that builds managed SaaS connectors for enterprise customers deploying LLM-powered features on hybrid clouds. They want an onramp for GPU-backed inference, options for private deployment (VPC/on-prem), reseller pricing, and security posture (SSO, KMS, SOC2). Interest in Redwood Dedicated for predictable performance and Redwood Private for regulated customers. Pilot requested to validate latency and cost.

Topics: 1) Partner integration model (reseller vs managed SI) 2) Deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) 3) Security and compliance (SAML, KMS, audit logs) 4) Pilot scoping and benchmarks 5) Commercial signals and timelines

[00:00] Jamie (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today, um we'll do a quick intros round and then Liam and Sofia will go into the technical surface area. Aisha, do you want to kick us off with a quick intro to QuartzWave?
[00:15] Aisha (QuartzWave): Sure yeah thanks Jamie. So QuartzWave — we do managed integrations for large SaaS customers, mostly in finance and health care, and we help them onboard GPU workloads into their VPCs and also provide a managed control plane. We're looking at partners to provide inference runtime, ideally something we can resell or bundle with our managed services.
[00:30] Marco (QuartzWave): Yep and to add — our typical customers require private deployments, data residency, and strict audit requirements. We have a few customers who will not accept public hosted APIs. So key for us is a Private or VPC offering from Redwood, and ability to run on the clouds we support (we do Azure, AWS, GCP) and some on prem.
[00:48] Liam (Redwood SE): Got it, thanks. Quick question on scale — what does a typical deployment footprint look like for these customers? GPUs per cluster, average QPS, latency targets?
[00:58] Priya (QuartzWave): Usually they want <200ms p95 for chat inference at 1024 tokens and throughput varies — one of our banking customers peaks at ~600 concurrent sessions, but often it's bursty. They also want model pinning, ability to roll back, and audit trails per request.
[01:18] Sofia (Redwood SE): Right — Redwood's Dedicated product can give you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, and Redwood Private sits inside your VPC with a customer-managed control plane. We support autoscaling policies and burst capacity. Small note: sometimes our doc generator says 'Redwood Dedicate' (laughs) so apologies for transcriptions.
[01:40] Marco: On that, how do you handle key management? Customers want to use their own KMS/HSM and manage encryption keys.
[01:48] Liam: We integrate with customer KMS providers — AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS — and we have an HSM option for Private deployments. All secrets for model artifacts can be stored encrypted and you can control the keys. There is also audit logging per request with trace IDs surfacing in the Console.
[02:10] Evan (Procurement): From a commercial perspective, can QuartzWave rebrand or bundle Redwood in our managed offering? Any reseller program?
[02:18] Jamie: Yes we have partner/reseller programs — need to loop in partnerships team, but high-level we support reseller SKUs and per-seat or committed capacity contracts for Dedicated. We'll follow up with program terms.
[02:30] Aisha: Great. On the tech side — quantization and kernel choices matter for our edge customers. Do you surface recommended quantization profiles?
[02:38] Sofia: Yup, Redwood Optimize gives model and quantization recommendations by workload, plus batching/caching suggestions to balance latency and cost. For some models we also have optimized kernels and compilation paths; if a customer is on older GPU families we can recommend different model variants or quantization to fit devices.
[03:00] Marco: Any caveats on continuous KV cache — our engineers are sensitive to token memory for long chats.
[03:06] Liam: We support KV cache management and prefix caching; you can evict or persist across sessions depending on the app. There's a tradeoff between latency and memory usage — we can set TTLs or per-tenant cache limits. Our runtime also does dynamic batching but respects latency SLOs.
[03:26] Priya: What's the shortest onboarding timeline you've done for a Private deployment? We have one client that wants a Q4 pilot inside a customer VPC, so timeline is tight.
[03:34] Sofia: For Private with a pre-approved infra pattern, we can do a minimum viable setup in 2–3 weeks if networking and KMS access are ready. Onboarding tends to be longer when there are strict audit controls or on-prem air-gapped requirements. For Dedicated hosted capacity it's faster — sometimes as little as a few days for a sandbox.
[03:54] Marco: Sounds good. For the pilot we want to validate: p95 latency at 1024 tokens, cost per 1k tokens, and behavior under burst load.
[04:04] Jamie: Good crisp success criteria. We'll capture that in the pilot plan. Liam — can you outline what you'd like from QuartzWave to scope infra?
[04:12] Liam: Sure — high level we need sample payloads (typical prompts), expected concurrency patterns, preferred model families, and any minimum latency targets. Also network diagrams for the VPCs and list of cloud regions. If you have compliance docs we should review early — SOC2 controls, legal agreements, any required encryption standards.
[04:32] Priya: We'll share a sample prompt set and a short perf spreadsheet. Any constraints around PCI/PHI workloads that we should know about?
[04:40] Liam: We have Private deployments certified to run workloads with PHI/PCI constraints when deployed in customer-controlled networks and with proper agreements; we'd want to review the specific compliance requirements.
[04:50] Aisha: A few practical questions — how do you handle rollouts and fallbacks? If a primary cluster gets saturated, does Redwood automatically failover to hosted or a lower-cost variant?
[04:58] Sofia: There's smart routing — you can define a policy to prefer Dedicated but failover to a hosted model variant or smaller model family when capacity is constrained. Rollouts support canary and A/B tests and automatic fallback policies.
[05:16] Marco: For benchmarking — do you provide tooling or do we run our own scripts?
[05:20] Liam: We have a perf harness and can share a script. We'll also run a side-by-side benchmark in a pilot. We'll drop links in the follow-up: perf script, deck, and a sample benchmark sheet.
[05:32] Jamie: I'll note the artifacts: Security pack link (redwood.com/security/partner-pack — placeholder), partner integration pack (drive link), perf spreadsheet (sheets link).
[05:40] Aisha: On pricing, can you share ballpark numbers for Dedicated per-GPU-hour and any reseller discounts? Our margins matter.
[05:48] Jamie: We'll send a pricing matrix — rough estimates now: per-GPU-hour depends on GPU class and committed term; reseller discounts are available for committed partners. We'll try to include a modeled cost for the pilot in the follow-up.
[06:02] Evan: Any minimum commitment for reseller onboarding?
[06:06] Jamie: Not for exploration/pilot. For production resale we typically expect a committed minimum for Dedicated pools, but we'll document options.
[06:14] Priya: One more — does Redwood support model licensing restrictions? Some of our customers require restrictive model licensing and tracing of model versions used per request.
[06:22] Sofia: Yes, model catalog and versioning supports pinning and audit logs include model id/version per request. We can also restrict which models are deployable in a given environment.
[06:34] Marco: Ok all sounding promising. Let's talk pilot shape: a 2-week pilot, dedicated 2-node GPU pool (NVIDIA-class), run our prompts at typical concurrency for a day to capture p95, and then a 24-hour soak test for burst. We also want cost numbers and the security review.
[06:52] Liam: That maps well. We'll propose specific GPU types and a config. Note: if you pick quantized models we can reduce cost by ~30–60% but may see slight quality diffs. We'll include suggestions.
[07:06] Aisha: Timing wise — can Redwood commit to starting the pilot in October?
[07:10] Jamie: We can target early October. I'll confirm after internal partner ops check and then we'll lock dates.
[07:18] Sofia: Action items recap — Liam will draft pilot infra and cost estimate; Sofia will upload perf harness; Jamie will send partner pack and pricing; Aisha to share NDA/agreement and sample prompts.
[07:30] Marco: Also want a technical deep dive during pilot — Marco + Liam to pair on network and KMS connectivity.
[07:36] Jamie: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[07:40] Priya: One small nit — do you support SAML-based SCIM provisioning for RBAC?
[07:46] Liam: Yes SAML and SCIM for user provisioning and RBAC hooks are supported in Console. We'll send the SSO checklist.
[07:56] Aisha: Great thanks everyone. We'll look out for the follow-up.
